This canvas organizes every course, program, module, lesson, question, learning outcome, assessment, simulation, delivery mode, audience description, and completion capability supplied for the Iron Vault Academy expansion.
The existing 320-lesson academy catalog remains the current base inventory and is not replaced by this expansion.
Repeated titles are consolidated into one canonical course while their appearances across multiple pathways are retained through cross-listing.
Spelling and naming are normalized (for example, zk-SNARKs and self-study).
Source-specific African positioning, including SACCO/chama use cases, is excluded from the general Iron Vault version.
Unsupported third-party certification, examination-voucher, tuition-credit, badge-percentage, and recognized-credential claims are excluded until a verified partnership exists.
Claims implying guaranteed or superior financial returns are replaced with neutral education about yield, borrowing, collateral, liquidation, and risk.
Iron Vault may issue its own course-completion certificate or digital completion credential based on verified completion data.

Course promise: Educate and empower learners to confidently discuss digital-asset technologies with their sector, clients, and colleagues.

Course description: This course introduces blockchain, Bitcoin, and distributed ledgers. Learners study how blockchain works, explore Bitcoin, review the technology’s history, and examine practical and emerging uses across finance and other business areas. The objective is to build a solid foundation for understanding how blockchain may affect operations, information safeguards, and industry structures.

Purpose: A technical avenue for developers, solution architects, technology enthusiasts, and professionals who want to build or deepen a blockchain-development career.

Recommended: at least one year of software-development experience in C++, Python, Java, or JavaScript. Solidity is influenced by C++, Python, and JavaScript. Foundation courses can be used as a bridge for learners who do not yet meet the recommendation.

Purpose: Translate the supplied DeFi-marketing material into a structured elective for founders, growth teams, and community operators.
Define what the project is, the problem it addresses, its tagline, its keywords, its differentiated value, and the audience that should care.
Analyze who the strategy is for. Separate newcomers, experienced users, builders, investors, operators, and institutional audiences rather than marketing to everyone.
Establish available budget before selecting tactics. Distinguish paid acquisition, content, partnerships, events, creators, community operations, and experimentation.

Evaluate influencer marketing, blockchain SEO, email, educational content, partnerships, community programs, airdrops where appropriate, and other distribution channels against the audience and budget.
Support early users, maintain communication, collect feedback, and convert community trust into long-term participation and advocacy.

Web3 growth requires project-specific positioning, audience clarity, disciplined resource allocation, channel testing, and sustained community engagement. Community is treated as a long-term operating asset, not a short-term promotional trick.
The curriculum is delivered through the three-part academy loop already established for Iron Vault: identity, training, and visible progress.
A persistent Vault identity associated with rank, progress, and earned achievements.
Quizzes, labs, simulations, scenarios, chain building, terminology matching, contract flows, and security decisions.
XP, levels, streaks, badges, course completion, pathway progress, and mastery milestones.
Collateral, interest, health-factor, and liquidation sandbox
Practice NFT mint and metadata exercise
Vulnerability recognition, exploit-path analysis, and remediation scenarios
Use XP as the internal learning-progress unit.
Award XP for first completion, improved assessment performance, verified labs, pathway milestones, and streaks according to documented rules.
Separate XP from any token, financial, or payout mechanism.
Use course-level pass requirements, retry policies, and prerequisite gates where the curriculum requires sequential mastery.
Award badges for demonstrated outcomes—not merely for opening content.
Record completion against a canonical course, module, lesson, interaction, and assessment identifier.

Items intentionally excluded from product claims
Unverified third-party exam vouchers, certification-board exam claims, certification-badge coverage percentages, and tuition-credit promises.
The Africa-specific positioning, including savings-group, SACCO, and chama framing, from the general-market curriculum.
Claims that DeFi yield will outperform bank interest or otherwise produce a particular financial result.
Any implication that course completion constitutes financial, legal, tax, or investment advice.
Import the existing 320-lesson inventory as the base catalog without renaming or deleting records.
Normalize every new item in this canvas into pathway, course, module, lesson, interaction, and assessment records.
Deduplicate shared courses through cross-listing rather than copying course content.
Assign stable identifiers and prerequisite relationships before UI implementation.
Map each interaction to Training Grounds and each verified completion event to Progress Vault.
Release the Eight-Week DeFi & Web3 Bootcamp as the first marketable guided journey while the deeper technical pathways are completed.

A trust-first public academy with a structured beginner entry point, practical DeFi journey, professional blockchain foundation, advanced Web3 developer pathway, AI career track, enterprise and security depth, and a single gamified learning system underneath it all.
